liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Franklin's Tower** (1 review): Franklin's Tower starts a bit dull but comes alive at several points [9]
- **Cassidy** (1 review): The Cassidy jam went very far out, then returned seamlessly, which astonished the reviewer [7]
- **Scarlet Begonias** (1 review): Scarlet Begonias into Fire on the Mountain sounded psychedelic and powerful, with a spacey feel [8]
- **Fire On The Mountain** (1 review): After his second big Fire solo, Garcia danced with arms raised and grinning, seen from the front row [11]
- **Estimated Prophet** (1 review): Estimated Prophet felt very eerie given the setting [11]
- **All Along The Watchtower** (1 review): The show fizzles out by the end, noticeably in the closing Watchtower [17]

## The recordings

- **gd1988-12-09.152145.ultramatrix.miller.flac1644** (recommended): soundboard; 19 songs; 142 min; rated 4.5/5 by 2 [1]
- **gd88-12-09.aud.willy.16093.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 19 songs; 139 min; rated 3.33/5 by 6 [2]
- **gd1988-12-09.152483.SennMKE2002.french.brown-onemoreshot.flac2496**: source not stated; 19 songs; 142 min [5]
- **gd88-12-09.set2-sbd.leeds.16465.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 11 songs; 82 min; rated 3.75/5 by 8 [6]. Said about its sound: Soundboard cymbals sound slightly dry and muffled; the electronic drums come across well and Mickey Hart sounds aggressive; Reviewer mixes audience tape for set one with soundboard for set two, because the soundboard only begins at set two [8][9]

## Around the show

- Venue felt like a fish tank; reviewer sat fifth row center, tickets bought via a roommate at a department store outlet [7]
- The band came into this show after 45 days without performing, and some rust showed [9]
- Santa Ana winds blew in Southern California that December; the reviewer flew out on short notice [10]
- Reviewer began a run of 115 straight shows here, lasting until 18 July 1990 at Deer Creek [10]
- The hills of LA were burning at the time, giving the song choices extra local resonance [11]
- Reviewer's van barely reached the camping parking lot; they watched from upper-level seats looking down on the band [15]
- Reviewer's first show, seated in the upper level, while a friend beside them danced throughout [16]
- In the second set Garcia flubbed lyrics and his solos meandered, while the crowd was hot [17]
- High Time was welcome but fell short of the past glory of Long Beach shows [12]
- High Time was welcome but fell short of the past glory of Long Beach shows [13]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1988-12-09.152145.ultramatrix.miller.flac1644**: taped by Steve Marcus; transferred by Mastered by Charlie Miller  March 27, 2021; source: UltraMatrix SBD > Cassette Master (Don Pearson) > Cassette (Dolby C) > WAV (16-bit/44.1k) [1]
- **gd88-12-09.aud.willy.16093.sbeok.shnf**: source: AUD>DAT>CD [2]. Also: Audience recording transferred AUD to DAT to CD, via Paul B, and seeded to etree by Willy [2]
- **gd1988-12-09.152483.SennMKE2002.french.brown-onemoreshot.flac2496**: taped by Ambient Master by Mike French "Moke".; transferred by Mike French, Scott Brown; source: Sennheiser MKE2002 omni's (x2) HRTF @ 6'4" -> Sony TC-D5M no dolby n.r.. From 16th row, center section, FOB,.. Not true center, but a few feet left of center.… [5]. Also: Taped with Neumann KM84i microphones, first generation patch from the OTS; the U.S. Blues encore is second generation [5]
- **gd88-12-09.set2-sbd.leeds.16465.sbeok.shnf**: source: Master Soundboard Cassette >DAT >CD [6]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Jerry Garcia: [1988-12-09 Grateful Dead Ticket - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/image/1988-12-09-grateful-dead-ticket/) [20]
